title: Actual whole-system comparison transition square and its two paths
statement: Fix the model family $D$ of [def-sp-field-shriek-system-models], the scalar/support evaluation coordinates of [def-sp-field-shriek-system-finite-laws], and the actual quotient reductions and coordinate isomorphisms of [def-sp-field-shriek-system-transitions]. For $E\le F$, $m\le n$, a fixed compactification, and a system $M$, with the quotient maps of [def-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-interfaces], define the first transition word by the balanced scalar reassociation of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], evaluation at $n$ of the actual system map $b(M)$, the target compact-support system\'s own reduction, and target evaluation at $m$. Define the second word by the other balanced reassociation, reduction of the source compact-support system, evaluation at $m$ of $b(M)$, and the same target coordinates. Define the whole-system transition-square predicate by equality of reduction after evaluation at $n$ of $b$ and evaluation at $m$ of $b$ after reduction of its source system. Finally, using the equality of the two coefficient ring maps, define the common finite word as the specified comparison of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], as defined in [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison], for $R_n\to S_m$, followed by compact support of scalar extension of the actual input-system reduction $r^M_{n,m}$, with the canonical balanced associator. These are definitions of words, without claiming their equality.
